findings.description: The smoke test replaces its real 120 ms wait with a write to the private `_map_overlay_last_refresh_msec` field followed by a single `process_frame`, so the refresh is forced to be due without the production throttle. The PR says this check already failed on the base and was not held against the change, so the edit changes how the failing test is driven rather than fixing its root cause in the production path.
findings.title: Overlay test bypasses the refresh timing gate

findings.description: `lanes_match` in `map_overlay_input_publication.cpp` runs a `memcmp` over every full wind and elevation column whenever the solve id does not match the last bake, which includes every daily solve. `read_map_overlay_inputs` then sets `out["same"]` from that scan, so a republished but unchanged wind field costs a full-map byte comparison before it can be skipped. This added scan is the equality check the rule forbids, and it also runs on every elevation refresh whose column array object changed.
findings.title: Wind refresh rescans unchanged columns

findings.description: The PR records that the macOS window probe received no draw callback, so the whole-frame time, P95 publication time, and actual frame time for the wind optimization were never measured in a player window. The documentation marks these as pending, but the rule requires that they be measured at 50× speed before the optimization is kept.
findings.title: Wind speed-up has no window frame timing

findings.description: The header row of the #66 table in feature-status.md has 9 cells, but its delimiter row `| --- | --- | ---: | ... |` has 10 columns. GitHub-flavoured Markdown needs the header and delimiter rows to have the same column count, so the table appears as raw pipe-separated text and readers of the evidence can't see the before/after counts lined up.
findings.title: New before/after count table will not render

findings.description: The new `note_wind_solve` path and the publication marker are added to the solver state, and the feature docs describe the solve id as costless, but no measured cost of maintaining the marker or its separate savings beyond shared encoding is recorded. The documented savings are only the overall overlay baseline counts, so a later reader cannot tell whether the marker itself costs more than it saves.
findings.title: Wind marker maintenance cost is not documented
